async def act(page):
    """
    Scroll to the bottom of the current homepage and attempt to navigate to page 2
    of the blog feed by clicking an accessible pagination link if one is revealed.
    Clicking a discovered pagination link is the last action because it will likely
    navigate away from the current page.
    """

    # Smoothly scroll to bottom in small steps to ensure lazy content loads
    previous_height = -1
    for _ in range(8):
        await page.evaluate("window.scrollBy(0, window.innerHeight)")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        # break early if we appear to be at or near the bottom
        height = await page.evaluate("document.body.scrollHeight")
        if height == previous_height:
            break
        previous_height = height

    # Ensure final jump to bottom
    await page.evaluate("window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)")
    await page.wait_for_timeout(500)

    # Common pagination link texts to try first (use get_by_role with name)
    candidates = [
        "2",
        "Page 2",
        "Next",
        "Next »",
        "Older",
        "Older posts",
        "Older Posts",
        "Older »",
        "»",
        "→",
        "Older →",
    ]

    for name in candidates:
        locator = page.get_by_role("link", name=name)
        if await locator.count() > 0:
            # Click the first matching pagination link (likely navigates away)
            await locator.first.click()
            return

    # Fallback: inspect all links for rel="next" or textual hints like 'next', 'older', or a plain '2'
    all_links = page.get_by_role("link")
    total = await all_links.count()
    for i in range(total):
        link = all_links.nth(i)
        try:
            text = (await link.inner_text()).strip()
        except Exception:
            text = ""
        try:
            rel = await link.get_attribute("rel")
        except Exception:
            rel = None

        if rel and "next" in (rel or "").lower():
            await link.click()
            return

        lower = text.lower()
        if lower == "2" or lower == "page 2" or lower.startswith("2") or "next" in lower or "older" in lower or text in {"»", "→"}:
            await link.click()
            return

    # If we reach here, no suitable pagination link was found; do nothing further
    return

2) Using the current page state (we are already on the homepage), avoid calling any knowledge-base helper because they all re-navigate to '/' and perform higher-level scraping; they don't provide a focused scroll-and-click action.
3) Scroll in repeated steps (and finally jump to bottom) so any lazily-rendered pagination controls become visible.
4) Try a list of common pagination link visible labels via accessibility-role selectors (page.get_by_role("link", name=...)). Each locator is guarded with await locator.count() before using .first() to avoid indexing errors.
5) If no direct named match is found, iterate all role="link" elements (checking count first) and inspect inner_text() and rel attribute in small try/except blocks; click a link whose rel contains "next" or whose visible text strongly indicates page-2/next/older.
6) Make the click the last action because it will likely navigate away from the page.
7) If no suitable link is found, return without navigating.
